description: Crawls content to train OpenAI's models.
robots_note: OpenAI documents GPTBot's IP ranges and states it honors robots.txt disallow rules.

description: Powers search-style results surfaced in ChatGPT.
robots_note: OpenAI states OAI-SearchBot respects robots.txt rules.

description: Fetches pages a user asks ChatGPT to browse in real time.
robots_note: OpenAI states ChatGPT-User honors robots.txt, though as a user-triggered fetcher it visits single pages rather than crawling.

description: Crawls content to train Anthropic's Claude models.
robots_note: Anthropic documents ClaudeBot and states it respects robots.txt directives and anti-circumvention signals.

description: Fetches pages on behalf of a user during a Claude conversation.
robots_note: Anthropic documents Claude-User alongside its other agents; it fetches single user-requested pages rather than crawling at scale.

description: Indexes content to inform Claude's search-style answers.
robots_note: Anthropic states Claude-SearchBot respects robots.txt directives.

description: Crawls and indexes pages for Perplexity's answer engine.
robots_note: Perplexity says PerplexityBot respects robots.txt, but independent investigations (notably Cloudflare's 2024–2025 reports) have observed undeclared fetching that bypassed blocks.

description: Fetches a page a user asks Perplexity to browse live.
robots_note: Perplexity's own documentation says Perplexity-User generally ignores robots.txt because fetches are user-requested.

description: Controls use of content for Gemini and Vertex AI training, separate from Googlebot.
robots_note: As a robots.txt token rather than a crawler, honoring your directive is its entire function; Google documents it officially.

description: Common Crawl's crawler; its dataset is widely used to train LLMs.
robots_note: Common Crawl is a nonprofit with a long public record of honoring robots.txt and crawl-delay directives.

description: ByteDance's crawler, used for training its AI models.
robots_note: ByteDance publishes no crawler documentation, and multiple independent reports have found Bytespider ignoring robots.txt; blocking it reliably requires firewall or CDN rules.

description: Controls use of content for training Apple's AI models (Apple Intelligence).
robots_note: Apple documents the token officially and honors it via Applebot's crawl infrastructure.

description: Crawls content for Amazon's search and AI products, including Alexa.
robots_note: Amazon documents Amazonbot and states it respects robots.txt, including wildcard rules.
crawl_delay_note: Amazon's documentation states plainly that Amazonbot does not support the crawl-delay directive. Rate-limit it at the server or CDN if it is crawling harder than you want.

description: Crawls content to train Meta's AI models.
robots_note: Meta documents the agent and states it respects robots.txt rules.

description: Cohere's crawler used for training and grounding its models.
robots_note: Cohere publishes no official crawler documentation, so robots.txt compliance can't be verified; use firewall rules if blocking it matters to you.

description: Apple's crawler powering Siri and Spotlight suggestions.
robots_note: Apple documents Applebot thoroughly and honors robots.txt directives.
crawl_delay_note: Apple's documentation states that Applebot does not follow crawl-delay, and that it adjusts its own rate instead to limit the load it puts on a site.

description: Google's generic crawler for research and internal product uses.
robots_note: Officially documented by Google and respects robots.txt like the rest of its crawler family.

description: Fetches pages when a Le Chat user's question requires them.
robots_note: Mistral documents the agent and states it respects robots.txt directives.

description: Fetches specific links for Meta AI when users share or request them.
robots_note: Meta's own documentation states Meta-ExternalFetcher may bypass robots.txt because fetches are performed on behalf of a user.

description: Crawls the web for the Allen Institute's open AI research models.
robots_note: Ai2 documents the crawler and honors robots.txt; as a research nonprofit it has strong incentives to stay compliant.

description: Fetches pages to generate DuckDuckGo's AI-assisted answers.
robots_note: DuckDuckGo documents the agent and states it respects robots.txt.

description: Crawls and fetches pages for You.com's AI search answers.
robots_note: You.com documents YouBot and states it fully respects robots.txt, including user-agent-specific rules. It caches robots.txt for 30 minutes, so a change takes up to half an hour to take effect.
crawl_delay_note: You.com's documentation states YouBot honors crawl-delay directives — one of the few AI crawlers that says so explicitly.

description: Huawei's Petal Search crawler, also feeding its AI products.
robots_note: Documented by Aspiegel/Huawei with published IP ranges; states it respects robots.txt and crawl-delay.

description: Extracts structured data from pages for customers, including AI companies.
robots_note: Diffbot's bulk crawling honors robots.txt, but customer-triggered, on-demand extraction of specific URLs has been reported to proceed regardless — treat blocks as advisory.

description: Crawls images across the web for Hive's visual-AI products.
robots_note: The bot is documented and states it respects robots.txt; blocking it mainly affects image collection.
crawl_delay_note: The Hive documents that ImagesiftBot supports crawl-delay, reading the value as the minimum number of seconds between the start of consecutive requests — it splits the day into intervals of that length and issues at most one request per interval.

description: Webz.io's crawler; its web-data feeds are sold to AI builders.
robots_note: Webz.io documents the bot and states it honors robots.txt; as a data vendor its compliance is part of its sales pitch.

description: Crawler for Timpi's decentralized search index.
robots_note: Timpi publishes limited crawler documentation; compliance reports are sparse. If blocking matters, verify behavior in your logs and back the block with a firewall rule.

description: Associated with training Huawei's PanGu large language models.
robots_note: No official documentation exists and independent compliance reports are limited — pair any robots.txt block with a firewall or CDN rule if opting out matters to you.
